To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a nano-CdSCdS/PS nanocomposite film with a nanoCdS loading of 10wt.% can be prepared by using a certain mercaptane as the surface modifier.
a highly filled nano-CdS/polystyrene nanocomposite film can be prepared when a certain mercapto compound is applied to the surface of the particles.

the nano-CdS particles can be modified by a certain mercaptans and the treated nanoparticles are able to form a highly filled composite with polystyrene, and that the self-organization of nanoparticles can be achieved in the composite.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication of highly filled nano-CdS/polymer composite films and the study of their photophysical properties.
the synthesis of nano-CdS with high crystallinity, the preparation of a highly loaded nano-CdS/polystyrene nanocomposite, and the study of the cooperative behavior of nano-CdSe in the composite.
the preparation of highly filled nano-CdS composite films with self-organization behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study is a significant contribution to the field of nanocomposites.
the nano-CdS modified by a certain mercaptans is a good candidate for the fabrication of nanocomposites.
the present approach is a novel method for the synthesis of nanocomposites with a high loading of nano-particles.

the self-organization of nanoparticles in polymer composites can be realized by surface modification of nanoparticles.
the self-organization of nano-CdS particles in the PS composite film is due to a strong electron transfer between the particles and the PS matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the self-assembly of the nanoparticles can be realized by using the strong interaction between the nanoparticles and the matrix polymer, which is different from the conventional self-assembly methods that use the weak interaction between the nanoparticles.
it may be possible to obtain a highly filled nano-CdS/polymer composite film with a loading as high as 20wt.% by using mercaptan-modified CdS as a precursor.
the electron transfer interaction can be a new and effective way to induce the self-organization of nanoparticles in nanocomposites.
